title: Który przypadek?
note: CASE-SELECTION UNIT, the first of five (codex/WHICH-CASE-SPEC.md, JAMES-LOCKED 2026-08-07). Exists because James reported he is not always sure which case to use: the gyms drill endings, nothing until now taught CHOOSING. TEACHES NOTHING NEW - teaches_structures [] and teaches_lemmas [] on the b1_two_futures / gym convention; every form on screen was verified against the position-aware pool for this node (make_pool.py --before a1_which_case, 866 lemmas). ORGANISED BY TRIGGER, not by case (locked decision 1): the governor is the thing the learner meets first in a real sentence, so the lesson is 'after nie ma / do / z / duzo / blisko -> Genitive', never 'the Genitive has six jobs'. INTRO TABLE IS DERIVED, NOT AUTHORED: slide 0's table is generated from data/case-map.json filtered to rows whose taught_by sits at or before path 44 - nine rows, five cases. TWO CASE-MAP DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS SAME COMMIT, both of which would have leaked untaught Polish onto an A1 screen (and into the Przypadki panel, which renders the same rows): (1) the quantity row read 'duzo - malo - blisko', but check_new.py puts malo at b1_adverb_comp [126], and there it is a degree adverb in the mniej/najmniej ladder, never a noun-governing quantifier - the row is now 'duzo - blisko', the two governors a1_gen_endings actually teaches, and no malo row was invented because the course never teaches it as a governor at all; (2) the naming row read 'to jest... / to sa...' under taught_by a1_gender, but 'to sa' is a2_plural_nom [56] and A1 owns no plural noun to put after it - the row is now 'to jest...' and a separate 'to sa...' row was added under a2_plural_nom, where it is true and where a2_which_case will pick it up. THE SPEC'S 'z ALREADY DOES TWO JOBS BY A1'S END' LINE WAS NOT WRITTEN, and this is the one place the unit departs from its brief: a1_prep_do_z teaches z + Genitive (origin) only, and z + Instrumental is a2_inst_z [64], so at path 44 z has exactly ONE job. Saying otherwise would be false at this position and would break the spec's own harder rule that cases the level has not taught appear nowhere. The two-jobs-of-z point is real and belongs to a2_which_case, which is where it lands. THE HONEST LINE the spec demands is carried on slide 1 in its A1-true half: w + Locative and do + Genitive are both 'place' in English and the case is still decided by the word in front, not by the meaning. Slide 3 adds the fact a selection unit is the right place for - domu / parku / banku / hotelu are the SAME STRING in the Genitive and the Locative, so on those nouns the trigger is the only thing that tells you which case you are in (precedent: a2_case_gym2's note names the same dual duty). KONTROLA is 8 form-choice items + 4 name-the-case items. The spec authorises both shapes ('name the case, or pick the right form'); the weighting is deliberate and conservative against AGENTS.md's 'real forms, not meta-questions' rule - naming the case IS this unit's teaching point rather than trivia about the language, but real forms still carry two thirds of the stage. Every distractor is a real, pool-legal Polish string; where a noun had only three taught forms the fourth choice is a different TRIGGER with its own correct form (duzo kawy / mam kawe / to jest kawa), which discriminates the governor rather than inventing a word. a1_case_gym's untaught 'kawie' distractor was NOT copied. One distractor was chosen against the obvious one: item 8 uses 'mam ksiazka' (plain wrong case, the a1_case_gym 'Mam kawa' precedent) rather than 'mam ksiazki', because ksiazki is the genitive singular here but becomes a correct nominative plural at a2_plural_nom, and marking it WRONG would plant a mis-learning the learner has to undo twelve units later. PISANIE is 12 mode:cloze items blanking the governed noun, exactly as the spec directs; every frame is a real sentence, so nothing is typed whole and the <=3-word cap is not in play. No duplicate answers: sklepie/sklepu and szkoly/szkole are deliberately paired so the same noun is produced in two cases against two triggers - that pairing IS the unit. UZYCIE is 12 whole sentences, each with a noun subject and/or object, and no sentence is shared with Pisanie. HOMOGRAPHS CHECKED, not assumed: kawy/wody/herbaty/szkoly/miasta/mleka taught as genitive singulars by a1_gen_endings and used as genitive singulars; ksiazki/apteki taught as genitive singulars by a1_gen_ki, and ksiazki appears only in the discussion above; miescie/sklepie/szkole/stole locatives; nauczycielem/lekarka/studentem/nauczycielka instrumentals from a1_inst_job. No plural anywhere - A1 owns none. The only adjective in the whole unit is 'dobra' inside the derived table's subject-row example (Kawa jest dobra.), which comes from case-map rather than from authoring; zgoda is declared in uses_structures for exactly that one cell and no other adjective was added, since the unit needs none and each would only add load.

intro.title: Five cases, and the word that chooses
intro.body:
Nothing in this unit is new. You have met all five cases already, one at a time, each inside the unit that taught its endings. What you have not met is the map.

Polish does not pick a case from what the sentence means in English. It picks from the word standing in front of the noun — the governor. Learn the governors and the case follows on its own.

Here is every trigger you own, and the case each one demands.

rows: the subject — who is doing it
a verb acting on a thing
w / na — meaning WHERE something is

intro.title: The trigger decides — not the English
intro.body:
This is the part that catches people out, and it is worth stating flatly.

w sklepie and do sklepu are both about a shop, and both are about place. English treats them as the same kind of phrase. Polish does not: w demands the Locative, do demands the Genitive, and the noun changes to match.

So the question to ask is never what the sentence means. It is which word is standing in front of the noun.
intro.body_pl: w sklepie → miejscownik · do sklepu → dopełniacz

rows: I'm coming back from the shop

intro.title: The Genitive has four triggers — more than any other case
intro.title_pl: Dopełniacz: nie ma · do · z/ze · dużo/blisko
intro.body:
At this level the Genitive is the case you reach for most often, because four separate triggers demand it and they have nothing in common in English.

Absence, destination, origin, quantity — four different jobs, one form. When any of these words appears, the noun behind it goes into the Genitive, with the endings you already drilled: masculine -u, neuter -a, feminine -y.
intro.body_pl: nie ma · do · z/ze · dużo/blisko → dopełniacz

rows: Piję dużo wody. · Sklep jest blisko banku.

intro.title: One form, two cases: domu, parku, banku, hotelu
intro.body:
A group of masculine nouns give you the same form for the Genitive and the Locative. That is a genuine simplification rather than a trap — provided you know it is happening.

do domu and w domu use the identical word domu, and the same holds for parku, banku and hotelu. The two cases are still different cases; the form simply does not show it. The trigger in front is the only thing telling you which one you are in, which is exactly what this unit is about.
intro.body_pl: do domu → dopełniacz · w domu → miejscownik

intro.title: The question to ask, every time
intro.body:
Before you put an ending on a noun, look to its left. One question, asked in the same order every time.

Is there a preposition? Then the preposition chooses: w and na for the Locative, do and z for the Genitive.

No preposition, but a verb? Then the verb chooses: mam, piję, chcę, lubię and kupuję take the Accusative, nie mam takes the Genitive, and jestem followed by a job takes the Instrumental.

Neither? Then the noun is naming something or doing something, and it stays in the Nominative — the form the dictionary gives you.
intro.body_pl: w/na → miejscownik · do/z → dopełniacz · mam/piję → biernik · jestem → narzędnik

rows: nothing — the noun names or acts

quiz.explain: w means where you are, and w always takes the Locative: sklepie. do and z point somewhere and take the Genitive instead.
Destination is do, and do takes the Genitive: szkoły. w szkole would say you are already there.

quiz.prompt: Coming back FROM there — the city →
quiz.explain: z is origin and takes the Genitive. miasto is neuter, so its Genitive is miasta.
piję acts on the tea, so the tea is the object: Accusative herbatę. The other three are real Polish — they are just answering different questions.
mam takes the Accusative, but nie mam takes the Genitive — the negation changes the case, not just the meaning.
dużo is a quantity word, and quantity words take the Genitive: wody.

quiz.prompt: You ARE one — a teacher (a man speaking) →
quiz.explain: jestem plus a job takes the Instrumental, so nauczyciel becomes nauczycielem. nauczycielką is the same case but the woman's word.
mam takes the Accusative, and a feminine noun swaps -a for -ę: książka → książkę.

quiz.prompt: Which case does w take, when it means where you are?
Which case do mam, piję and lubię take?
Which case does jestem take, when you name your job?
